Build a TanStack Start application with file-based TanStack Router routes, validated search params, route loaders, typed server functions, full-document SSR, and streaming. Keep server-only work behind explicit boundaries, choose the appropriate SSR mode per route, and target the deployment runtime without changing the application model.

# Convex setup

Set up Convex in the current folder. Run the commands yourself, without asking the user.

- Empty folder: `pnpm create convex@latest . -- -t bare`
- Convex project (`convex` in `package.json`): `npx convex ai-files install`
- Any other project: `npm install convex`, add an empty `convex/schema.ts` and a `convex dev` script, then `npx convex ai-files install`. Never `npm create convex` here, it replaces the folder.

* Also add Tanstack srart as the the project framework usign the command avoe
* 

Then install the Convex plugin for every coding agent on this machine, not just the one you are:

- Claude Code (`claude` on PATH): `claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, then `claude plugin install convex@claude-plugins-official --scope user`
- Codex (`codex` on PATH): `codex plugin marketplace add get-convex/convex-codex-plugin`, then `codex plugin add convex@convex-codex-plugin`

Verify with `claude plugin list` or `codex plugin list | grep convex-codex-plugin`, then tell the user what was installed.

how is --cmd different from the other one?

<pasted_content id="f44d">
--cmd <command>
Command to run as part of deploying your app (e.g. vite build). This command can depend on the environment variables specified in --cmd-url-env-var-name being set.

--cmd-url-env-var-name <name>
Environment variable name to set Convex deployment URL (e.g. VITE_CONVEX_URL) when using --cmd
</pasted_content id="f44d">

They don't do the same job. `--cmd` is the build step you want to run, and `--cmd-url-env-var-name` is only the name of the variable that build step reads.

- **`--cmd <command>`:** this is the command `convex deploy` runs after it pushes your Convex functions, for example `pnpm run build`. While it runs, the Convex deployment URL is in its environment, so your frontend build can read it.
- **`--cmd-url-env-var-name <name>`:** this names that variable, for example `VITE_CONVEX_URL`. It only matters when you use `--cmd`, and it changes nothing by itself.

You can usually leave out `--cmd-url-env-var-name`. Convex detects common frameworks and picks the right name, including `VITE_CONVEX_URL` for Vite, which this project uses. Add it only if detection picks the wrong name or your code reads a different one, like this:

```bash
npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm run build' --cmd-url-env-var-name VITE_CONVEX_URL
```

# Story-time: shared experiences & moments

## Context
Story-time lets people share experiences and moments with others, privately by default: every piece of personal data is
opt-in and entered by the user, never harvested from the OAuth profile. Backend is Convex (+ local components),
media on Cloudflare R2, mail via Cloudflare Email Service, frontend is TanStack Start + shadcn deployed to Cloudflare Workers.
Today `Story-time/` is a bare TanStack Start + Vite+ scaffold (empty `convex/schema.ts`, no Convex link, no auth, no shadcn).
This plan covers backend + the `/home` → `/e/$id/new` flow. URL previews ("preview") are a later phase.

## Decisions (confirmed)
- **Auth**: `@convex-dev/auth@2.0.0-alpha.x` (v2, component-based; alpha, API may break, no upgrade guarantee). GitHub + Google only, via `setupCore/setupGithub/setupGoogle`; users table is app-owned (`setupCore({usersTable})`). v2 ships `./react`, `./server`, `./browser` but **no TanStack adapter** → thin one written by us.
- **Region**: per experience. One Convex deployment per region (US default, EU `aws-eu-west-1`, AU `aws-ap-southeast-2`, CA `aws-ca-central-1`; non-US = +30% cost; a deployment's region can't change).
- **Encryption**: server-side keys. R2 **SSE-C** + field-level AES-GCM for sensitive fields.
- Assumptions to correct if wrong: "events" = the shared experience (`/e/$id`); "sessions" = per-viewer share grants with a Revoke button (not login sessions, those live in the auth component).

## Data model (`convex/schema.ts`)
- `users` (app-owned; auth core creates rows via `createUser` → inserts `{}`): all optional — `displayName`, `imageFileId`, `region` ('us'|'eu'|'au'|'ca', default 'us'), `locale`. OAuth profile fields are **not** copied.
- `events`: `ownerId`, `title`, `description?`, `startsAt?`, `endsAt?`, `status` ('draft'|'active'|'archived'), `visibility` ('private'|'invite'), `region`, `momentLimit` (default 10), `momentCount`, `keyVersion`, `coverMediaId?`. Indexes `by_owner`, search on `title`.
- `moments`: `eventId`, `authorId`, `startsAt`, `place?` (encrypted {name, lat?, lng?}), `blocks[]` — union of `photo{mediaId}`, `link{url, title?, note?}`, `note{text}`, `feeling{text, mood?}`; encrypted fields stored as `{iv, ct, v}`. Index `by_event_startsAt`.
- `itinerary`: one denormalised row per moment — `eventId`, `momentId`, `startsAt`, `dayKey`, `monthKey`, `placeKey` (hash of place, not plaintext), `position`. Indexes `by_event_day`, `by_event_month`, `by_event_place`. Written only by moment mutations; the UI groups by `?groupBy=day|place|month`.
- `media`: `eventId`, `momentId?`, `uploaderId`, `r2Key`, `size` (≤5 MB), `mime`, `sha256`, `keyVersion`, `status` ('reserved'|'ready').
